answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce token in a shared vault before it may submit a claim; after a challenge period, the token is returned only if the claim survives a randomly selected audit. A sybil operator must therefore tie up capital for every identity and risks losing it when identities forge evidence or coordinate false claims. The delay and audit cost make mass identities expensive, while honest agents can reuse their returned stake; shale can name the network’s underlying resource without changing this rule.
